newsitem.title: DUBAI: Arab airlines need 150 new jets in next 5 years.
newsitem.headline: Arab airlines need 150 new jets in next 5 years.

text.p: Arab airlines will need to buy 150 new aircraft for an estimated $15 billion over the next five years to help modernise their fleet and meet growing demand, an Arab airline official said on Wednesday.

Arab Air Transport Federation Secretary-General Abdul-Wahab Toufaha told a news conference on the sidelines of an aviation conference in Dubai that the new jets would replace some of the ageing aircraft or meet airlines' future expansion needs.
His remarks were carried by several Gulf news agencies.
Toufaha said that the 17 Arab airlines who are members in the federation need to change at least 59 aircraft. They have a total of 405 aircraft of various types and models.

Toufaha said he expected airlines to register a four percent growth in passenger traffic by the end of the year, from a seven percent growth in 1995 due to "negative" political developments that affected the volatile region.
This included "the stalled Arab-Israeli peace process that led to a regression in the number of tourists visiting the region and cut the number of passangers," he said.

Renewed Iraqi-American tension in September and the election victory of Israel's hardline Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in May slammed breaks not only on peace talls but also on the growth of regional tourism, Arab tourism officials said.
Toufaha said most Arab airlines will also be affected by the rise in international fuel prices this year, which increased their operational costs by at least five percent.
Many have raised prices by three percent in line with a recommendation made by the International Air Transport Association last month to cushion the effect of fuel rises.
